note: Off-gate timing evidence for the two corpus executables. Not a gate: no threshold, no assertion, nothing here is a contract. See bench/run.py for what a number here does and does not mean.

workloads.note: Zero vectors: process start, runtime init, reading an empty file and exiting, with no corpus work at all. The floor every marginal cost below is measured against, and the reason a raw time ratio sits below the work ratio.

The 20-vector worked corpus the contracts replay. Carries no prefix series: 5, 10 and 20 vectors all sit inside the startup floor, so ratios across it would measure noise and process startup rather than the corpus.
The first 17,598 of the corpus's 70,390 vectors.
The whole corpus, handed to the binary in place rather than copied.

The growth series' base: the same 17,598 vectors as generated-quarter, under its own label. The two are byte-identical on purpose, so the pair also reads as a repeatability check taken at two points in the same run.
The base vectors twice: 35,196 vectors of exactly the base's mixture, so the work ratio is exactly 2.0 and no part of the time ratio comes from the corpus changing shape.
The base vectors four times: 70,392 vectors, within 0.01% of the whole corpus's vector count and made of one quarter only.

series.name: prefix
series.note: Prefixes of the corpus, read as a size series; the mixture is not constant across them, because the corpus's first quarter holds 8.2 MB of its 15.8 MB.

series.name: growth
series.note: One fixed set of vectors repeated 1x, 2x, 4x: volume doubles with the mixture held exactly constant, so this is the series the complexity question is read from.
